title: Visual Designer
dek: Birdwatch produces three weekly newsletters and a growing slate of sponsored content. You'd design the visual language that has to hold across all of it.
description: Birdwatch Media publishes independent newsletters covering urban planning, climate policy, and local news for three mid-size cities. We're small — nine people total — and visual design has mostly been done ad hoc by whoever had time, which means our sponsored-content pieces don't look consistent with each other, let alone with the editorial newsletters.

You'd own the visual production for sponsor placements and one-off illustrated pieces, working directly with our editor-in-chief and two staff writers. A typical week involves building a header illustration or data visualization for a feature story, formatting a sponsor's content to feel native rather than bolted-on, and slowly building out a shared style guide so the next hire doesn't start from zero.

This is a hands-on production role more than a strategic one, at least at first — you'll be making a lot of things, fast, on tight editorial deadlines. There's real room to grow into art direction as the company adds headcount, but the day-to-day right now is execution.
requirements: 1–3 years of visual or editorial design experience — agency, in-house, or a strong freelance portfolio all count
Comfortable with fast turnaround work; some pieces go from brief to published same-day
Solid typography and layout fundamentals — this is a newsletter company, so most of the work is fundamentally about reading
Illustration or basic data-visualization skills are a strong plus, not required
Adobe Creative Suite or Figma; we're flexible on tooling as long as output is clean
